correctness.rationale: Decomposition AW=WT+UF and independent Gaussian blocks gives G^{-1}HF. Conditional on all but the ith Gaussian column of G, each error entry is ||f_j|| times the ratio of independent complex N(0,1) variables. The ratio density is 1/[π(1+|z|^2)^2]; a real component has CDF [1+x/sqrt(1+x²)]/2. The transformed median-of-three component is 3(1-u²)du/4 and has variance 1/2; summing real and imaginary component variances yields one per entry. No independence across different entries is assumed. For the m+1-row sketch, the two-dimensional Schur complement is Gamma(2,1) and E inverse is 1, yielding expected trace m. Direct independent symbolic rational calculation checks the median moment. If E=0, all errors vanish; otherwise the square ratio has logarithmically divergent second moment.
residual_risks: Exact expectation statement does not imply eigenvalue or eigenvector accuracy, numerical conditioning or sample-level unitary invariance.

value.rationale: The natural square Gaussian Ritz sketch has infinite Frobenius risk; a minimal three-replicate median restores finite risk and exactly matches one extra least-squares row. Exact efficiency/robustness benchmark of practical numerical linear algebra relevance, with explicit cost caveat.
residual_risks: Three square sketches may require more projections and solves than a single slightly oversampled rectangular solve; no runtime superiority claim.

final_claim: For independent standard circular complex Gaussian square sketches, componentwise complex coordinate medians over three randomized Ritz compressions have mean squared Frobenius error m||E||_F^2, exactly equal to a single (m+1)-row least-squares sketch; a lone square sketch has infinite squared risk if E≠0.
limitations: Complex iid circular Gaussians, exact arithmetic, orthonormal W and entrywise medians; no spectral/eigenpair error, floating point, real Gaussian, or equivariance conclusion.
